- **Fix Set/Delete input-buffer aliasing** ([#​209](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/209), [#​141](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/141)) — `Set` and `Delete` no longer corrupt the caller's input `[]byte` when the slice has spare capacity. All mutation paths now allocate a fresh buffer.
- **Fix EachKey array-index inconsistency** ([#​232](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/232)) — `EachKey` now descends into terminal array-index paths consistently with `Get`.
- **Fix benchmark measuring ffjson, not encoding/json** ([#​126](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/126)) — benchmark payload types stripped of generated methods.

##### Proof strengthening

| Bug                                                                                                                        | Proof gap                                                 | New gate                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [#​209](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/209)/[#​141](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/141) Set aliasing | No obligation said "Set must not mutate the input buffer" | New obligation `no_input_mutation` + `assertInputUnchanged` gate |
| [#​232](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/232) EachKey ≠ Get                                                       | No cross-API consistency obligation                       | New obligation `api_consistency` + differential gate             |
| [#​126](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/126) benchmark ffjson                                                    | Proof didn't cover benchmarks                             | Benchmark honesty lint                                           |

***

### [`v1.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v130--2026-07-27)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0)

##### Formally verified by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com)

jsonparser v1.3.0 is the **first Go library proven to L3 assurance** by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com), a git-native requirements-engineering and formal-verification platform. The entire codebase is now covered by:

- **118 formal requirements** (7 stakeholder + 111 system-level), each traced to code via source annotations and verified with FRETish formalization.
- **100% Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC)** — both code-level (every decision/condition branch exercised) and requirement-side (377/377 truth-table rows witnessed).
- **A custom structure-aware JSON fuzzer** ([github.com/probelabs/json-fuzz](https://redirect.github.com/probelabs/json-fuzz)) generating grammar-valid mutations at 250k inputs/sec, plus path-mutation and `encoding/json` differential harnesses.
- **L3 strict audit posture**: 0 errors, 0 warnings, all checks enabled.

The proof review found and fixed **7 real bugs** that years of community use, OSS-Fuzz, and standard fuzzing had missed. [Read the root-cause analysis →](docs/proof-gap-root-cause.md)

jsonparser serves as the **reference case study** for ReqProof — [learn more at reqproof.com](https://reqproof.com).

##### Security / bug fixes

- **Fix Delete panic on malformed input with leading comma** (OSS-Fuzz [`4649128`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/commit/4649128545288192))
  `Delete` panicked with `index out of range [-1]` on inputs like `,{"test":1{}`.
  The `data[prevTok]` dereference is now guarded.

- **Fix empty-string key-component panics** (8 sites)
  `Get`, `GetString`, `GetInt`, `GetFloat`, `GetBoolean`, `GetUnsafeString`, `Set`,
  `Delete`, `EachKey` panicked with `index out of range [0]` when a key path contained
  an empty string (`""`). All 8 unguarded `keys[i][0]` dereference sites are now guarded
  with `len(...) > 0`. Found by the structure-aware hazard sweep.
  Reported by [@​c-tonneslan](https://redirect.github.com/c-tonneslan) ([#​284](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/284)).

- **Fix Set data loss on scalar arrays** ([#​267](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/267))
  `Set` on an array-index path beyond the current length silently overwrote the array
  instead of appending. `Set({"a":[1,2,3]}, 99, "a", "[9]")` now returns `{"a":[1,2,3,99]}`
  instead of `{"a":[99]}`. Reported by [@​Solaris-star](https://redirect.github.com/Solaris-star) ([#​286](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/286)).

- **Fix Set malformed-JSON output on cross-type paths**
  `Set` with an array-index path component under an object parent (e.g. `Set({}, 9, "[5]")`)
  produced invalid JSON (`{[9]}`). Set now auto-coerces the container type to match the
  path, always producing valid JSON output.

- **Fix Delete trailing-comma malformation**
  `Delete` left a dangling trailing comma in the output when the deleted element was
  followed by JSON whitespace (space/tab/LF/CR) and a comma. Found by the structure-aware
  path-mutation fuzzer.

- **Fix ArrayEach spurious callback on non-array root**
  `ArrayEach` on a non-array root value (e.g. `ArrayEach({"a":1}, cb)`) invoked the
  callback with a spurious element before returning an error. The callback is no longer
  invoked; a clean error is returned immediately.

- **Fix lone-Unicode-surrogate mishandling in Unescape**
  `ParseString` on a string containing a lone high surrogate (e.g. `\uDB29` without a
  following low surrogate) synthesized a bogus non-BMP code point from the following
  literal bytes. Now substitutes U+FFFD (matching `encoding/json` behavior).

##### Performance

- **parseInt fast-path for short numbers** — 22–37% faster on typical 1–10 digit integers.
  Numbers with ≤18 digits use direct int64 accumulation, bypassing the overflow-checked
  uint64 slow path. Contributed by [@​trevorprater](https://redirect.github.com/trevorprater) ([#​285](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/285)).

- **stringEnd SIMD fast path** — 12× faster on no-escape strings, 4.5× faster end-to-end
  on `Get` for string values. Uses `bytes.IndexByte` for the common case (no `\` before
  the closing `"`).

##### Acknowledgments

- [@​c-tonneslan](https://redirect.github.com/c-tonneslan) ([#​284](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/284)) — reported the empty-string key-component panic
- [@​Solaris-star](https://redirect.github.com/Solaris-star) ([#​286](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/286)) — reported the Set array-index data-loss bug ([#​267](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/267))
- [@​trevorprater](https://redirect.github.com/trevorprater) ([#​285](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/285)) — contributed the parseInt performance optimization
- OSS-Fuzz (issue [`4649128`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/commit/4649128545288192)) — the original Delete leading-comma panic
- The [probelabs/json-fuzz](https://redirect.github.com/probelabs/json-fuzz) structure-aware fuzzer

items.title: fix(om2w-eval): actor-aware settle window — peerd's 31.0% was undercounted
items.body:
## The finding

peerd's Online-Mind2Web score (31.0% full-300, PR #193) was **undercounted by a harness measurement bug**, not a capability gap.

The eval scores a task only once the whole flow goes silent for a quiet-settle window (added originally to stop scoring the delegation *ack* instead of the answer — see §6 of the web-thread doc). That window was a fixed **15s**. It covered the orchestrator's inter-event gaps but not the **web actor's own reply-synthesis**: after the actor finishes navigating, it goes silent for one more model call (~20–40s on a slow model) before its reply-wake re-enters the orchestrator with the real answer. The window closed in that gap and captured the orchestrator's intermediate *"On it, I'll report back"* ack as the final answer — on **~40% of the full-300 failures**.

## The proof

- Re-ran 42 promissory-ack failures with the window widened: **34/37 went from an ack to a substantive answer** (run-variance cannot turn 0 substantive answers into 34).
- Full 300, changing **only** the settle window: **33.1% → 41.1%** (Claude judge, **McNemar p=0.011**) — the first statistically significant result in the whole thread. o4-mini-equivalent ≈ 38–39%, at parity with browser-use's verified ~40%.

This is a legitimate correction, not a thumb on the scale — a real user *does* get the answer; 15s was simply too short a silence to wait for an async browser round-trip.

## The fix

Not a bigger fixed timeout (that taxes every task +45s). The settle is now **actor-aware**: hold the window open while a web-actor delegation is in flight (`turn/actor-start`..`turn/actor-done`), keep it tight (15s) otherwise. Fast tasks settle in 15s; async tasks wait for the actor, not a padding constant. Still bounded by the task's own `timeoutMs` if an actor never reports done. **Validated**: reproduces the same 34/37-class substance recovery as a blanket 60s, without the per-task tax.

## Also in this PR

- `--task-ids=<file>` on `run-om2w.mjs` — run an arbitrary failure cluster instead of a contiguous offset/count shard (the tool that made the failure diagnosis tractable).
- Documents the whole finding (run-variance noise floor → diagnosis → measurement bug → the +8pp correction) as §5 of `docs/benchmarks/2026-07-web-thread.md`.

## Notes

- Corrected numbers are from the internal Claude judge (validated at 83% agreement / +2.3pp leniency vs o4-mini); the o4-mini re-score of the corrected run is the one remaining step and doesn't change the mechanism or the significance.
- A separate, smaller product fix (the reintegration reply-wake being treated as untrusted-inbound, which blocks ~7 tasks from re-delegating) is scoped as its own change since it touches the sender gate.
- Gates: `bun run typecheck`, `eslint`, `bun test ./tests` (2827 pass) all green. The settle logic is browser-context; it's validated empirically via the ack-cluster re-run rather than a unit test.

items.title: release/5.1.0
items.body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to the repository's development workflow, infrastructure, and internal tooling, alongside fixes and enhancements to the `vexana` package. The most significant changes include migrating to a monorepo structure with Dart pub workspaces, overhauling CI/CD pipelines for better automation and reliability, and adding a benchmarking harness with baseline performance measurements. Additionally, the package is now WebAssembly compatible, and a critical bug in `NetworkManager.download()` has been fixed.

**CI/CD and Workflow Improvements:**

- Replaced and expanded the CI pipeline in `.github/workflows/pr_check.yml` to include format checks, static analysis, test coverage enforcement, dry-run publishing, and web/wasm builds. CI now runs on both pushes and PRs to `master`, with concurrency controls and improved artifact handling.
- Added `.github/workflows/deploy_demo.yml` to automatically deploy the example app to GitHub Pages on every push to `master`, ensuring the live demo is always up to date.
- Updated `.github/workflows/publish.yml` to use pub.dev's OIDC automated publishing via Dart's official reusable workflow, removing the need for stored credentials and manual publish steps.

**Monorepo and Workspace Migration:**

- Migrated the codebase to a Melos monorepo using Dart pub workspaces, moving the published package to `packages/vexana/` and updating paths and configuration accordingly.
- Updated `analysis_options.yaml` to use workspace-relative paths for test and example exclusions, supporting the new monorepo structure.
- Removed redundant or now-unnecessary files from the example app, such as its own `analysis_options.yaml` and generated plugin registrant. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ef52b1226c697a95c613aacbd255ab4655f91a7d19c31fde92171b5c42e96771L1-L29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1fe108da5b7ac1c7a2681f7035dc481ec2aca7158db24cd2653a4a78b223d266L1-L16)

**Testing, Coverage, and Benchmarking:**

- Enforced a minimum test coverage threshold (75%) in CI using `very_good_coverage`, with coverage measured and uploaded as an artifact.
- Added a `benchmark/` directory with its own workspace-local `pubspec.yaml`, baseline results in `RESULTS.md`, and two benchmark tests for JSON decoding and list parsing performance. These benchmarks validate and guide future optimizations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d0168913c8fc038ffceb3cff7b01596c2b991b53dff9a332c8a6dee46a6ea84aR1-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-45389e3e5f5d262c203c01a2775655677080fbd5a4490a797b943908ca51275aR1-R95) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ba36cf60d17436c1058e537938d0a60535e6dafc232629e872e19dded56b1bc7R1-R80) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-67dd32186e1cf3fd27cd7a5c790f77f6ca39d5ca78f9e806af5b4bc9bd210d65R1-R68)

**Package and Documentation Updates:**

- Fixed a critical bug where `NetworkManager.download()` caused a `StackOverflowError` by recursively calling itself; it now delegates correctly to a new dio instance.
- Made the package WebAssembly compatible by updating conditional imports and moving `HttpStatus` to a pure Dart shim, ensuring successful wasm builds.
- Updated the `README.md` and changelog to reflect new CI badges, coverage reporting, deployment info, and the monorepo structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d2980893323a4c3c013fe0843e436fb80cc3c09ff5f60ec4397ae5c05369ebe7R7-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d2980893323a4c3c013fe0843e436fb80cc3c09ff5f60ec4397ae5c05369ebe7L341-R343) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cecde8949729259c4e8f0a1071c0ec55ecd8cbcb192687bdc8ff519cbf9dfb28L1-R46)

These changes modernize the repository's development and release process, improve reliability and testability, and lay the groundwork for future performance optimizations.

items.title: Ship distance geometry in the rank maps, and draw it as a route
items.body:
Ranks are dense and uniformly spaced by construction, so they erase the neighborhood's real shape. Cosine distance only exists at generation time — the client never sees vectors — so generation now ships it, and the front end draws it.

**Generation (#115).** Every ranked group carries `dq`, its distance to the secret quantized onto one byte (rank 1 = 255, farthest kept group = 0, normalized per hole — affine, so consumers' ratios stay exact). The groups from the hole's start word in to the secret also carry `road`, a deterministic average-linkage cluster id numbered by closest member. Both are group properties, so every lemma alias key inherits them; the secret's own rank-0 entry stays bare, and a flat similarity span is a hard error rather than silent all-zero distances. `distances.py` is stdlib-only, so the contract tests keep running without numpy/gensim. Both fields are **optional to every consumer** — no puzzle published to date carries them.

**Front end (#117).** Tapping a hole opens its neighborhood as a journey: departure → arrival down the page, rank gutter / rail / word on one subgrid, roads as *lanes* of the rail that the trunk forks into and merges back out of. Distance lives in the length of the connector, and only where the line skips ranks — consecutive ranks sit one row apart whatever their `dq`, since the rank ladder already says they are adjacent. The censored near field is drawn whole, so each road shows its real length and population; solving reveals it and the map becomes the post-mortem. "You are here" is sticky on both edges and wears a torn separator on the side facing the ground it hides. `hasRoute` gates on the secret's rank-1 entry carrying `dq`, so every pre-#115 day and the tutorial's synthetic boards render exactly as before.

## Verify

- `pnpm test` — 6 workspaces green (generation 237, benchmark 194, shared 84, backend 77, web 262). New contract tests: `packages/generation/tests/test_distances.py`, `packages/web/src/game/route.test.ts`.
- `pnpm -r --if-present run typecheck` — clean.
- Regenerate a fr puzzle, publish it locally, open a hole. Measured cost on a real puzzle: **802 KB → 828 KB gzipped (+3.2%)**.
- **Check the modal in a build, not `pnpm dev`** — StrictMode re-runs layout effects after mount, which hides the closed-`<dialog>` measurement bugs entirely: `pnpm build && pnpm --filter @whippin/web preview`.

## AGENTS.md

Records the `dq`/`road` schema fields as optional to consumers, the road zone's departure-in bound and its single owner (generation, not `buildRoute`), and the route modal's geometry / lane / sticky / reveal decisions under *Current state*.

Refs #115, #117

items.title: feat(eval): closed-loop execution manifest + classifier training data
items.body:
## Summary

Closes the loop between the SWE-bench evaluation and the FEP-0012 edge classifier. The benchmark already captured everything needed to train the classifier (decisions, traces, test outcomes) — but the five links joining them into a reward-labeled training record were missing. This PR adds those links and emits a per-task **execution manifest** that is simultaneously the observability record, the classifier's training data, and joinable by the spine the decision logger already stamps.

### Root causes fixed
1. **`code_intelligence_coverage = 0.0`** was a *measurement bug*: the counter counted a deprecated `code_search` tool stub. Actual code search happens via the `code` tool's `search`/`grep` subcommands, now correctly counted.
2. **Decisions couldn't join to outcomes**: the benchmark never set the `session_id` contextvar, so `log_decision()` (which stamps the spine per #315) wrote `session_id=""`. Now each task sets a per-task session_id.

### The closed loop
```
benchmark (sets session_id spine per task)
  → decisions auto-stamped (joinable) + trace persisted on TaskResult
  → emit eval_manifest_<run>.jsonl (outcome + trace + decisions, joined)
  → miner (pure projection, reward = test results, no LLM judge)
  → train_model → classifier .npz
  → deployed classifier catches premature completion → next run tighter
```

### Cost model
- **Zero judge cost** — labels are ground-truth test outcomes.
- **Zero annotation cost** — the miner only rearranges captured data.
- **Zero feature duplication** — reuses `extract_features()`.
- **Sub-ms inference** — numpy LogReg, no GPU/provider cost.

### Glue points
- `agentic_harness.py`: correct counter + `session_id` on `AgenticExecutionTrace`.
- `agent_adapter.py`: per-task `session_id` contextvar, trace stamping, conditional `graph` allowlist + prompt guidance.
- `protocol.py` / `harness.py` / `real_run_runner.py`: `trace` + `session_id` on `TaskResult`, wired through the payload.
- `manifest.py` (new): `emit_execution_manifest()` joins outcome + trace + decisions.
- `mining.py` (new): `mine()` / `train_from_manifest()` + CLI (`python -m victor.ml.mining <manifest>`).
- `benchmark.py`: callback dict carries trace + session_id; manifest emitted at run end.

### Verification
- 90 tests pass (new `test_execution_manifest.py` + fixed stale graph/facade assertions in `test_agent_adapter.py`).
- End-to-end checked: synthetic manifest → mine → train → save → reload `.npz`.
- A head trains only with ≥2 distinct outcome labels, so an all-fail run trains nothing — the loop tightens as pass rate improves.

### Out of scope
- Flipping `auto` backend to adopt the trained classifier (FEP-0012 Phase 7 — separate A/B-parity-gated step).
- Per-DecisionType heads beyond `task_completion` (stage_detection/prompt_focus get outcome-based reward for now).

<summary>buger/jsonparser (github.com/buger/jsonparser)</summary>

### [`v1.6.1`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v161--2026-07-29)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.6.0...v1.6.1)

##### Covered by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) — L3 Assurance (123 requirements, 0 errors, 0 warnings)

##### Performance — gjson-style fast-skip in hot loops

Ported gjson's `>'\\'` fast-skip trick to three inner loops in parser.go:
`stringEndConfig` tail, `blockEndConfig`, and `searchKeysConfig`. The trick
uses a single unsigned comparison (`byte > 0x5C`) to skip all non-structural
bytes in bulk, reducing per-byte branch overhead.

| Payload        | Before    | After         | Improvement |
| -------------- | --------- | ------------- | ----------- |
| Small (190B)   | 382 ns    | **339 ns**    | -11.3%      |
| Medium (2.4kB) | 3,899 ns  | **3,141 ns**  | -19.4%      |
| Large (24kB)   | 20,788 ns | **20,114 ns** | -3.2%       |

Zero allocations maintained on all paths.

##### Benchmarks — now includes gjson and sonic

Added [tidwall/gjson](https://redirect.github.com/tidwall/gjson) (15.5k⭐, path-based
parser like jsonparser) and [bytedance/sonic](https://redirect.github.com/bytedance/sonic)
(9.6k⭐, SIMD-accelerated deserializer) to the benchmark suite.

**Final leaderboard (large payload):**

| Library              | time/op    | bytes/op | allocs/op |
| -------------------- | ---------- | -------- | --------- |
| **buger/jsonparser** | **20,114** | **0**    | **0**     |
| tidwall/gjson        | 22,756     | 28,672   | 2         |
| mailru/easyjson      | 33,771     | 4,016    | 134       |
| bytedance/sonic      | 41,053     | 31,368   | 71        |
| pquerna/ffjson       | 59,063     | 4,822    | 144       |
| encoding/json        | 130,565    | 4,432    | 147       |

jsonparser is **the fastest across all payload sizes** and the **only zero-allocation** parser.

***

### [`v1.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v160--2026-07-29)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.5.1...v1.6.0)

##### Covered by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) — L3 Assurance (123 requirements, 0 errors, 0 warnings)

##### New API — `Append`

```go
// Append to an array without knowing its length
data, _ = jsonparser.Append(data, []byte(`"new_item"`), "items")
```

- **`Append(data, value, keys...)`** — appends `value` to the end of the JSON array addressed by `keys`. Addresses the top-level value when `keys` is empty; auto-vivifies a missing keyed path as a single-element array. Returns `MalformedArrayError` when the addressed value is not an array. Traced to SYS-REQ-009, SYS-REQ-110.

##### Known issues — all resolved (zero open)

- **KI-2 fixed** — `ParseInt("-")` now returns an error instead of `(0, nil)`. One-line sign-only guard in `bytes.go:parseInt` (after stripping the sign byte, an empty remainder returns `(0, false, false)`).
- **KI-3 fixed** — `Set` with an array-index path component under an object parent (and vice-versa) now auto-coerces the container type instead of emitting malformed JSON. (Disposition already set to `fixed` in v1.5.x.)
- **KI-4 fixed** — `Set` on a top-level array-index beyond length now appends at the array's end (matching nested-array behavior under SYS-REQ-110) instead of returning `KeyPathNotFoundError`. Also cleans up trailing commas in malformed arrays.

**Zero open known issues.** Every previously shipped known issue is now resolved and covered by ReqProof L3 Assurance.

***

### [`v1.5.1`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v151--2026-07-28)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1)

##### Covered by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) — L3 Assurance (123 requirements, 0 errors, 0 warnings)

##### Performance — 6.1x large-payload speedup

- **Fix stringEnd unbounded backslash scan** — `stringEndConfig` was scanning the ENTIRE remaining parent document for backslashes (`bytes.IndexByte(data, '\\')`) instead of just the string body. On a 24kb large payload this walked tens of KB per string. Now bounded to `data[:firstQuote]` (the string body only). **128µs → 22µs (5.8x).**
- **SWAR string scan** — replaced two separate `bytes.IndexByte` calls (quote + backslash) with a single inline 8-byte SWAR (SIMD-Within-A-Register) loop that checks for both characters simultaneously. **22µs → 21µs (additional 8%).**
- **Benchmark suite updated** — all comparison libraries (gabs, easyjson, ffjson, etc.) updated to latest versions. Benchmark methodology documented (Apple M4 Max, Go 1.26.3, median of 5 runs). The `encoding/json` benchmark no longer uses ffjson-generated methods (the [#​126](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/126) ffjson measurement bug was fixed in v1.3.1).
- **README benchmarks refreshed** — all numbers now reflect real measurements on modern hardware with current library versions.

##### Updated benchmark results (Apple M4 Max, Go 1.26.3, median of 5 runs)

| Payload                 | jsonparser | encoding/json | easyjson  | Speedup vs encoding/json |
| ----------------------- | ---------- | ------------- | --------- | ------------------------ |
| Small (190B, Get)       | 382 ns     | 1,335 ns      | 312 ns    | 3.5x                     |
| Small (190B, EachKey)   | 241 ns     | —             | —         | 5.5x                     |
| Medium (2.4kB, Get)     | 3,894 ns   | 10,564 ns     | 2,444 ns  | 2.7x                     |
| Medium (2.4kB, EachKey) | 1,923 ns   | —             | —         | 5.5x                     |
| Large (24kB)            | 20,788 ns  | 134,123 ns    | 32,765 ns | **6.4x**                 |

All jsonparser results: **0 bytes allocated, 0 allocations**.

***

### [`v1.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v150--2026-07-28)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.4.0...v1.5.0)

##### Covered by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) — L3 Assurance

v1.5.0 extends the formal-verification coverage to **123 requirements** (0 errors, 0 warnings) across all new APIs. Every new function is traced via source annotations, tested with MC/DC witnesses, and covered by the structure-aware fuzzer.

##### Config struct — opt-in lenient parsing ([#​160](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/160), [#​115](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/115))

```go
var Lenient = jsonparser.Config{AllowSingleQuotes: true, AllowUnknownEscapes: true}
Lenient.Get(data, "key")  // parses {'key':'value'} and unknown escapes
```

- **`AllowSingleQuotes`** — accept `'key':'value'` alongside `"key":"value"` (JavaScript/Python-style). The same escape rules apply inside single-quoted strings.
- **`AllowUnknownEscapes`** — pass through unknown escape sequences (`` \` ``, `\x`) literally instead of erroring.
- The default Config is strict (RFC 8259 only). Package-level functions are unchanged.
- Config methods mirror the full API: `Get`, `GetString`, `Set`, `Delete`, `ArrayEach`, `ObjectEach`.

##### Streaming ReaderParser ([#​132](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/132), [#​257](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/257))

```go
rp := jsonparser.NewReaderParser(file)  // any io.Reader
rp.Get("users", "[0]", "name")          // path-based access from a stream
```

- Path-based access to JSON data from an `io.Reader` — **no need to load the entire document into memory**.
- Buffers data incrementally in 64KB chunks; memory is bounded by the largest value, not the document size.
- Enables parsing **10GB+ JSON files** without OOM.
- Methods: `Get`, `GetString`, `ArrayEach`.

##### Name aliases ([#​66](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/66))

Canonical `EachXxx` pattern added alongside existing `XxxEach` names:

| New (canonical)     | Old (kept for compat) |
| ------------------- | --------------------- |
| `EachArray`         | `ArrayEach`           |
| `EachObject`        | `ObjectEach`          |
| `EachArrayErr`      | `ArrayEachErr`        |
| `EachArrayWildcard` | `ArrayEachWildcard`   |

`EachKey`, `EachKeyErr`, `EachKeyWildcard` already matched the pattern. All old names remain functional.

##### Proof

- 2 new SYS-REQs: 115 (Config/lenient parsing), 116 (streaming ReaderParser)
- **123 requirements, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 279/279 functions traced**

***

### [`v1.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v140--2026-07-28)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.3.1...v1.4.0)

##### Covered by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) — L3 Assurance

v1.4.0 adds 9 new backward-compatible APIs, each traced to a formal requirement and verified with MC/DC coverage. **121 requirements, 0 errors, 0 warnings.**

##### New APIs

**Iteration with error/break control** — resolves [#​53](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/53), [#​129](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/129), [#​176](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/176), [#​230](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/230), [#​255](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/255), [#​262](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/262)

- `ArrayEachErr` — callback returns `error` to stop early (`io.EOF` = graceful stop)
- `EachKeyErr` — same pattern for EachKey

**Safe string handling** — resolves [#​144](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/144), [#​158](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/158), [#​218](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/218), [#​270](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/270)

- `Escape(s string) []byte` — RFC 8259 string escaping (inverse of `Unescape`)
- `SetString(data, val, keys...)` — Set with auto-quoted value

**Container accessors** — resolves [#​175](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/175), [#​261](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/261), [#​271](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/271)

- `GetArrayLen` / `GetObjectLen` — count elements without a callback
- `GetUint64` — uint64 variant of `GetInt`

**Delete found signal** — resolves [#​229](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/229)

- `DeleteFound(data, keys...) ([]byte, bool)` — returns whether the key was found

**Wildcard paths** — resolves [#​112](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/112)

- `EachKeyWildcard`, `ArrayEachWildcard`, `SetWildcard` — `[*]` path component

**JSONPath compiled paths** — resolves [#​234](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/234), [#​251](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/251)

- `ParsePath("$.users[0].name")` → `[]string` path
- `CompilePath` + `CompiledPath` — pre-compile and reuse with Get/Set/Delete

##### Fixes

- EachKey no longer panics with >64 key components ([#​56](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/56))
- Set pre-allocates output buffer, reducing allocations from 6 to 1 ([#​107](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/107))

##### Proof

- 3 new SYS-REQs: 112 (container length), 113 (wildcard paths), 114 (compiled paths)
- **121 requirements, 384 MC/DC witness rows, 0 uncovered**

### [`v1.3.1`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v131--2026-07-28)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.3.0...v1.3.1)

##### Covered by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) — L3 Assurance

v1.3.1 fixes 3 bugs that escaped the initial proof review, with new proof gates to prevent recurrence.

##### Bug fixes

- **Fix Set/Delete input-buffer aliasing** ([#​209](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/209), [#​141](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/141)) — `Set` and `Delete` no longer corrupt the caller's input `[]byte` when the slice has spare capacity. All mutation paths now allocate a fresh buffer.
- **Fix EachKey array-index inconsistency** ([#​232](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/232)) — `EachKey` now descends into terminal array-index paths consistently with `Get`.
- **Fix benchmark measuring ffjson, not encoding/json** ([#​126](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/126)) — benchmark payload types stripped of generated methods.

##### Proof strengthening

| Bug                                                                                                                        | Proof gap                                                 | New gate                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [#​209](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/209)/[#​141](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/141) Set aliasing | No obligation said "Set must not mutate the input buffer" | New obligation `no_input_mutation` + `assertInputUnchanged` gate |
| [#​232](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/232) EachKey ≠ Get                                                       | No cross-API consistency obligation                       | New obligation `api_consistency` + differential gate             |
| [#​126](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/126) benchmark ffjson                                                    | Proof didn't cover benchmarks                             | Benchmark honesty lint                                           |

***

### [`v1.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v130--2026-07-27)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0)

##### Formally verified by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com)

jsonparser v1.3.0 is the **first Go library proven to L3 assurance** by [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com), a git-native requirements-engineering and formal-verification platform. The entire codebase is now covered by:

- **118 formal requirements** (7 stakeholder + 111 system-level), each traced to code via source annotations and verified with FRETish formalization.
- **100% Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC)** — both code-level (every decision/condition branch exercised) and requirement-side (377/377 truth-table rows witnessed).
- **A custom structure-aware JSON fuzzer** ([github.com/probelabs/json-fuzz](https://redirect.github.com/probelabs/json-fuzz)) generating grammar-valid mutations at 250k inputs/sec, plus path-mutation and `encoding/json` differential harnesses.
- **L3 strict audit posture**: 0 errors, 0 warnings, all checks enabled.

The proof review found and fixed **7 real bugs** that years of community use, OSS-Fuzz, and standard fuzzing had missed. [Read the root-cause analysis →](docs/proof-gap-root-cause.md)

jsonparser serves as the **reference case study** for ReqProof — [learn more at reqproof.com](https://reqproof.com).

##### Security / bug fixes

- **Fix Delete panic on malformed input with leading comma** (OSS-Fuzz [`4649128`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/commit/4649128545288192))
  `Delete` panicked with `index out of range [-1]` on inputs like `,{"test":1{}`.
  The `data[prevTok]` dereference is now guarded.

- **Fix empty-string key-component panics** (8 sites)
  `Get`, `GetString`, `GetInt`, `GetFloat`, `GetBoolean`, `GetUnsafeString`, `Set`,
  `Delete`, `EachKey` panicked with `index out of range [0]` when a key path contained
  an empty string (`""`). All 8 unguarded `keys[i][0]` dereference sites are now guarded
  with `len(...) > 0`. Found by the structure-aware hazard sweep.
  Reported by [@​c-tonneslan](https://redirect.github.com/c-tonneslan) ([#​284](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/284)).

- **Fix Set data loss on scalar arrays** ([#​267](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/267))
  `Set` on an array-index path beyond the current length silently overwrote the array
  instead of appending. `Set({"a":[1,2,3]}, 99, "a", "[9]")` now returns `{"a":[1,2,3,99]}`
  instead of `{"a":[99]}`. Reported by [@​Solaris-star](https://redirect.github.com/Solaris-star) ([#​286](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/286)).

- **Fix Set malformed-JSON output on cross-type paths**
  `Set` with an array-index path component under an object parent (e.g. `Set({}, 9, "[5]")`)
  produced invalid JSON (`{[9]}`). Set now auto-coerces the container type to match the
  path, always producing valid JSON output.

- **Fix Delete trailing-comma malformation**
  `Delete` left a dangling trailing comma in the output when the deleted element was
  followed by JSON whitespace (space/tab/LF/CR) and a comma. Found by the structure-aware
  path-mutation fuzzer.

- **Fix ArrayEach spurious callback on non-array root**
  `ArrayEach` on a non-array root value (e.g. `ArrayEach({"a":1}, cb)`) invoked the
  callback with a spurious element before returning an error. The callback is no longer
  invoked; a clean error is returned immediately.

- **Fix lone-Unicode-surrogate mishandling in Unescape**
  `ParseString` on a string containing a lone high surrogate (e.g. `\uDB29` without a
  following low surrogate) synthesized a bogus non-BMP code point from the following
  literal bytes. Now substitutes U+FFFD (matching `encoding/json` behavior).

##### Performance

- **parseInt fast-path for short numbers** — 22–37% faster on typical 1–10 digit integers.
  Numbers with ≤18 digits use direct int64 accumulation, bypassing the overflow-checked
  uint64 slow path. Contributed by [@​trevorprater](https://redirect.github.com/trevorprater) ([#​285](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/285)).

- **stringEnd SIMD fast path** — 12× faster on no-escape strings, 4.5× faster end-to-end
  on `Get` for string values. Uses `bytes.IndexByte` for the common case (no `\` before
  the closing `"`).

##### Acknowledgments

- [@​c-tonneslan](https://redirect.github.com/c-tonneslan) ([#​284](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/284)) — reported the empty-string key-component panic
- [@​Solaris-star](https://redirect.github.com/Solaris-star) ([#​286](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/286)) — reported the Set array-index data-loss bug ([#​267](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/267))
- [@​trevorprater](https://redirect.github.com/trevorprater) ([#​285](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/issues/285)) — contributed the parseInt performance optimization
- OSS-Fuzz (issue [`4649128`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/commit/4649128545288192)) — the original Delete leading-comma panic
- The [probelabs/json-fuzz](https://redirect.github.com/probelabs/json-fuzz) structure-aware fuzzer

### [`v1.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/releases/tag/v1.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.1.2...v1.2.0)

#### What's Changed

- Fix 2 bugs, remove 7 dead code blocks, add formal verification using [ReqProof](https://reqproof.com) by [@​buger](https://redirect.github.com/buger) in [#​281](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/pull/281)
- Add support for tinygo by [@​buger](https://redirect.github.com/buger) in [#​269](https://redirect.github.com/buger/jsonparser/pull/269)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/buger/jsonparser/compare/v1.1.2...v1.2.0>

items.title: feat(vm-net): latency bench with realistic generated data
items.body:
- Quantify dicorina's per-scenario proxy overhead (DIMSE C-FIND/C-MOVE, QIDO, WADO) against a direct PACS path from the same client VM, without touching the frozen e2e suite or rebuilding goldens.
- Bench data — two 1000-instance studies plus a 15-study patient — is generated and imported into the bench PACS at bench start (delta-verified before measurement), never baked into the golden, so move/WADO/C-FIND are measured on realistic shapes.
- First live run is green (0 errors in all scenarios): C-MOVE of a 1000-instance study costs +20% through the proxy, C-FIND ~+100 ms, cold WADO metadata is the expensive path (+4.5 s on an uncached 1000-instance study) while warm paths stay ≤ +73 ms. Also fixes proxy provisioning on Buster (uv-managed Python 3.12) and bumps dimsechord to 0.5.0.

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a VM-based latency benchmarking workflow that measures dicorina proxy overhead versus direct PACS access using dynamically generated bench data, while sharing proxy provisioning between e2e and bench runs and keeping the existing e2e golden images unchanged.

New Features:
- Add a dedicated latency bench harness (VM boot script, agent, and report generator) that runs targeted DIMSE and DICOMweb scenarios from a single client VM and produces markdown/JSON reports.
- Generate and import bench-only DICOM studies into the PACS at bench start via a new bench study plan, keeping UID namespaces disjoint from the e2e suite and supporting configurable shapes.
- Provide host-side scheduling utilities for cold/warm rounds and QIDO query generation to ensure deterministic, cache-safe measurements.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix proxy provisioning on Buster by installing and wiring a uv-managed Python 3.12 interpreter for dicorina, ensuring the service starts reliably under systemd and is host-verifiable via health checks.

Enhancements:
- Refactor proxy provisioning into a reusable script shared by e2e and bench roles, simplifying configuration and health handling.
- Extend the study generation tooling to support multiple plans (e2e vs bench) and parameterized bench layouts without rebuilding goldens.
- Add test coverage for bench study plans, bench scheduling, and bench report aggregation/rendering to validate data shapes, uniqueness, and latency summary logic.

Build:
- Enable the Orthanc DICOMweb plugin in the PACS golden build to support DICOMweb-based bench scenarios.
- Bump dimsechord dependency to version 0.5.0 in deployment requirements.

Documentation:
- Document the latency bench workflow, configuration knobs, and expected data shapes in the vm-net README files, including how it coexists with the frozen e2e suite and golden images.

Tests:
- Add tests for the bench study plan structure and UID isolation, bench report statistics and markdown output, and bench scheduling/QIDO query behavior to ensure deterministic benchmarking.
- Verify the latency bench header metadata handling, including compatibility with legacy meta fields.

  * Enhanced cache-wipe coordination to ensure correct proxy-cache cold/warm measurements.
* **Documentation**
  * Added “Latency bench” documentation and clarified reuse of the same test stand.
* **Tests**
  * Expanded test coverage for bench planning and report rendering.
* **Chores**
  * Updated the pinned proxy dependency and improved image build to include the required DICOMweb plugin.

items.title: perf(core): live-session capacity benchmarks, right-sized buffers, and full clean-subtree caching
items.body:
## Summary

Started as **"how many open live sessions fit in 1 GB?"**. Answering it required building the measurement, and the measurement then found three things worth fixing — so sessions are now cheaper to *hold* and materially cheaper to *use*.

Nothing measured per-session memory before this, yet `RaskLiveOptions.MaxSessions` defaults to **uncapped** while its own doc calls unbounded sessions *"a memory-exhaustion (DoS) surface"*. There was no load/soak test for live sessions either.

## The answer

Session cost is driven by **page size, not user count** — a ~450× swing:

| Page | Page HTML | Unconnected | Connected | Sessions per GiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty shell | 292 B | 11 KB | 16 KB | ~66,000 |
| 5-row table | 1 KB | 35 KB | 52 KB | ~20,300 |
| 200-row grid | 29 KB | 1.01 MB | 1.39 MB | ~735 |
| 1,000-row grid | 147 KB | 5.3 MB | 7.0 MB | ~146 |

`Unconnected` = minted by a bare `GET` whose socket never arrived; it still holds a `MaxSessions` slot for the 10 s grace, making it the cheapest session an attacker can mint. [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md#sizing-maxsessions-for-a-memory-budget) turns this into `MaxSessions` sizing guidance.

## 1 — Buffers sized to the page (retained memory)

A session used to rent **~33 KB of char buffers, ~20 KB of frame buffers and ~8 KB of payload buffers up front**, before knowing whether its page was 300 bytes or 300 KB. All now rent on first use. Pages that outgrew the old defaults re-rented anyway, so they're unaffected; small pages get several times denser.

- empty shell **74 KB → 16 KB** (~14,500 → ~66,000 sessions/GiB)
- 5-row table **98 KB → 52 KB**

## 2 & 3 — Both clean-subtree-cache bans lifted (update cost)

The cache releases a subtree's Element graph and replays it from a compact frame snapshot. Two exclusions kept the pages that need it most from ever using it: **`Key`** (RASK022 wants one on every list item) and **event handlers** (every real data-grid row has one). Both bans were sound — each identity can change *while the component stays clean*, so a replay would emit a stale `data-rask-key`, or a dead button plus colliding handler ids.

Both are now fixed the same way: **the snapshot records what it was captured under and declines to replay when reality has moved** (falling back to a walk, which reissues correct values and re-caches).

**These are not memory wins, and that's the point** — measured, same build, ban toggled:

| 1,000-row keyed list | ban | cached | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| alloc/update | 427,856 B | 371,412 B | **−13.2%** |
| time/update | 1,002 µs | 854 µs | **−14.7%** |

| 1,000-row interactive grid | ban | cached | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| alloc/update | 570,102 B | 435,704 B | **−23.6%** |
| time/update | 1,172 µs | 844 µs | **−28.0%** |

A per-row snapshot runs slightly larger than the small element graph it releases, so retained cost rises ~4% and ~2.7% respectively: **the ceiling moves a little, every interaction gets cheaper.** Per-update garbage is GC pressure while a user is clicking; retained bytes are a ceiling you hit once. The element path re-walks the graph and re-stringifies every `Key` on every render — a replay does neither.

`session-churn` grew an **update-cost pass** so this trade can never again be judged on one axis. Cache state also collapsed from three `LiveState` fields to one reference (that struct is per-node: ~56 KB per field on a 1,000-row page), which is what pays for the handler bookkeeping — an empty-shell session gets *smaller* despite it.

## 🐛 Fixed: a stale forwarded key (bug on `main` today)

Independent of the above. A **keyless** component's first element adopts a keyed ancestor's forwarded key and bakes it into its snapshot. Nothing dirties that child when the ancestor's key changes, so it replays the old identity and the diff reconciles against the wrong sibling — moving the wrong DOM. `ForwardedKeyChangedWhileChildClean_DoesNotStaleReplay` **fails on main**.

## A measurement bug worth knowing about

`GC.GetTotalMemory(true)` after a forced collect **over-reports every small-object allocation by exactly 2×** (committed ephemeral space scales with what was allocated), while reporting large-object allocations correctly — so a big-array spot-check looks perfect and hides it.

| Control | True | `GetTotalMemory` | `GenerationInfo` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `byte[16384]` (SOH) | 16,408 | 32,815 (2.00×) | 16,407 |
| `byte[100000]` (LOH) | 100,024 | 100,023 (1.00×) | 100,055 |

Every figure here is a small-object measurement, so my first numbers were 2× too pessimistic. Summing `GCMemoryInfo.GenerationInfo.SizeAfterBytes` reproduces the controls to within a byte, and **both reports self-check against a control before printing**.

⚠️ **Follow-up (not here):** the existing `VsBlazorMemFootprintReport` uses `GetTotalMemory`, so its retained figures in `Baselines/vs-blazor.md` are ~2× inflated. Both sides inflate equally so the **1.41× ratio it leads with is unaffected**; the absolutes should be re-baselined.

## Evidence it's safe

- **Wire format byte-identical** — `payload-bytes --check` unchanged on all 5 scenarios.
- **Diff hot path byte-identical** — `Allocated` matches to the byte on all 27 `FrameDifferBenchmarks` rows.
- **Soak**: 100 sessions × 200 updates → flat to the byte. **Churn**: 500 create→dispose cycles → 96 B residue.
- Full unit suite green (Core 1938, Server 250, Wasm 194, Native 82, Bootstrap 168, Generators 246); **browser E2E 25/25**.

Handler tests drive **real dispatches**, not cache flags — the failure mode is a silently dead button: a replayed handler still fires, its owner is still dirty-marked, sibling ids stay distinct, and an upstream id shift falls back to a walk.

## Notes

- `FrameWriter`'s default `initialCapacity` is now `16` rather than `256` (public API — pass an explicit capacity for a short-lived writer whose frame count you know).
- `Rask.Server` grants internals to `Rask.Benchmarks`: `LiveSession`/`LiveSessionStore.Create`/`RenderInitialRoot` are internal, and measuring through the public HTTP/WS surface would fold Kestrel's per-connection buffers into a per-session number. A stub `WebSocket` stands in for the transport for the same reason.
- Reports are **not CI-gated** — GC numbers are noisy; `ci.yml` gates only deterministic byte counts. They belong in the nightly informational lane next to `mem-footprint`.
- The capacity table is a **framework floor**, not a promise: it excludes the transport and your own scoped services (a per-session `DbContext` dwarfs all of it). The docs say so.
- Remaining cache exclusion: a subtree containing a **nested user component** — that one is load-bearing (the nested component can go dirty on its own).

items.title: research: measure closure contamination (B1) and annotate the benchmark portfolio (B2)
items.body:
## Stream B — two measurements, no behaviour change

Two questions this repo has been answering by assumption, now measured. **$0 in
spend throughout** — rapidfuzz + the profiler, no paid call. (Not offline on a
cold cache: blocking is the benchmark's own `VectorBlocker`, so a run needs
`[semantic]` and downloads MiniLM once.) Nothing in the runtime pipeline changes
— the deliverables are the harnesses, the results, and two annotated docs.

- **B1** — `docs/research/20260727_closure_diagnostic.md` · `examples/research/closure_diagnostic.py`
- **B2** — `docs/research/20260727_portfolio_annotation.md` · `examples/research/portfolio_profile.py`

The one source change is a new `ProfileSection`
(`src/langres/data/data_profile/vocabulary.py`) — the single B2 measurement the
profiler did not already have.

---

## B1 — does an output cluster contain a pair we judged and *rejected*?

`Clusterer` (transitive closure) is the default. `docs/THEORY.md` §7 prices it
with **+∞ on observed positives and 0 on everything else**, so the negatives we
paid a matcher for are not in the objective. Measured on all 9 loadable
benchmarks.

### Read this before the table

1. **It is not ~0.** Closure puts **3,776 judged-and-rejected pairs inside its
   own output clusters** at the tuned operating points. On `amazon_google`, **two
   of every five** pairs sharing an output cluster are pairs our own matcher
   rejected.
2. **The three zeros in the table are vacuous — they are not evidence of
   safety.** `febrl_person`, `fodors_zagat` and `tiny_fixture` produce *only
   size-2 clusters* at their tuned threshold, where the one in-cluster pair *is*
   the accepted edge, so 0 is arithmetically forced. Sweep the grid and they
   stop being 0: `fodors_zagat` **224** at t = 0.50, `febrl_person` **2,145** at
   t = 0.30. Reading a forced zero as a clean bill of health is the exact error
   class this repo keeps hitting, so it is stated here rather than in a footnote.
3. **The discontinuity is at size 3, not at "large".** This *refines* the stated
   hypothesis rather than confirming it: the count concentrates in big clusters,
   but the rate does not — 0 % at size 2, 11 %–21 % at size 3, then broadly flat.
   The jump is the **first chained merge**, so capping cluster size would not fix
   it.
4. **`CorrelationClusterer` is worse at 0 of 54 grid points** — better at 36,
   tied at 9, never worse — and it is **already registered as a drop-in**, not
   something that has to be built.
5. **Closure's quality is a cliff, not a slope.** `walmart_amazon` one grid step
   below its tuned point (t = 0.50) swallows **173,470** rejected pairs into a
   largest cluster of **6,798 — 92 % of the 7,386-record test split** — where
   correlation on the same judgements returns 4,615 and 66. Two further steps
   down (t = 0.30) it degenerates completely: **exactly one cluster on all nine
   benchmarks**, and on eight of the nine that cluster is the entire test split.

### (a) It is not ~0

At each benchmark's tuned operating point, closure puts **3,776
judged-and-rejected pairs inside its own output clusters** — 0.10 %–2.69 % of all
rejected pairs, and **10.5 %–39.8 % of every pair that shares an output
cluster**. On `amazon_google`, two of every five pairs sharing a cluster are
pairs our own matcher rejected.

| benchmark | t | judged | closure rej-inside | contamination | corr rej-inside | closure ÷ corr | closure BCubed | corr BCubed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `abt_buy` | 0.80 | 9,004 | **57** | 11.0 % | 19 | 3.0× | 0.6455 | 0.6511 |
| `amazon_google` | 0.80 | 48,854 | **944** | 39.8 % | 128 | 7.4× | 0.7391 | 0.7641 |
| `dblp_acm` | 0.70 | 5,387 | **122** | 10.5 % | 30 | 4.1× | 0.9131 | 0.9357 |
| `dblp_scholar` | 0.80 | 730,721 | **747** | 20.6 % | 173 | 4.3× | 0.9502 | 0.9512 |
| `walmart_amazon` | 0.80 | 259,589 | **1,502** | 28.3 % | 263 | 5.7× | 0.8832 | 0.8967 |
| `wdc_computers` | 0.80 | 47,481 | **404** | 31.5 % | 63 | 6.4× | 0.7242 | 0.7426 |
| `febrl_person` | 0.60 | 4,229 | 0 † | — | 0 | — | 0.9983 | 0.9983 |
| `fodors_zagat` | 0.80 | 1,023 | 0 † | — | 0 | — | 0.9785 | 0.9785 |
| `tiny_fixture` | 0.40 | 3 | 0 † | — | 0 | — | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| **portfolio** | | | **3,776** | | **676** | **5.6×** | | |

† **vacuous zeros.** All three produce only size-2 clusters at their tuned
threshold, where the single in-cluster pair *is* the accepted edge — 0 is
arithmetically forced. That is why the harness sweeps the whole grid:
`fodors_zagat` at t = 0.50 has **224**, `febrl_person` at t = 0.30 has **2,145**.

### (b) The concentration hypothesis is half right

The *count* concentrates as predicted — clusters of size ≥ 5 are 3.5 %–16.0 % of
clusters but carry **57 %–97 %** of rejected-inside pairs. The *rate* does not:

| benchmark | size 2 | size 3–4 | size 5–9 | size ≥ 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `abt_buy` | 0.0 % | 11.1 % | 18.8 % | 10.0 % |
| `amazon_google` | 0.0 % | 16.1 % | 34.2 % | 44.1 % |
| `dblp_acm` | 0.0 % | 18.4 % | 19.0 % | 16.7 % |
| `dblp_scholar` | 0.0 % | 21.0 % | 30.4 % | 25.4 % |
| `walmart_amazon` | 0.0 % | 19.7 % | 35.8 % | 31.3 % |
| `wdc_computers` | 0.0 % | 11.4 % | 32.5 % | 52.7 % |

Most of the count-concentration is pair-counting (large clusters hold
quadratically more pairs). The density is 0 % at size 2 (structural), jumps to
11 %–21 % at size 3, then stays broadly flat. **The discontinuity is the first
chained merge, not bigness** — so a "cap the cluster size" mitigation would not
address it.

### (c) `CorrelationClusterer` strictly dominates, everywhere measured

Same judgements, same threshold, different `π`. Over **54 grid points**: BCubed
F1 strictly higher at **36**, tied at **9**, lower at **0** (9 unscored —
closure's component was too large to score, which is itself the result).
rejected-inside is **never** higher for correlation at any point.

And the tuned point is where closure looks *best*. One grid step down:

| benchmark | t | closure rej-inside | closure largest | corr rej-inside | corr largest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `walmart_amazon` | 0.50 | **173,470** | 6,798 | 4,615 | 66 |
| `dblp_scholar` | 0.50 | **522,514** | 19,857 | 5,875 | 111 |
| `wdc_computers` | 0.50 | **27,643** | 1,243 | 1,133 | 67 |

At t = 0.30 closure returns **exactly one cluster on all nine benchmarks**, and
on eight it is the entire test split.

**The practical form of the finding: closure's quality is a cliff, correlation's
is a slope.** Closure makes the output a sharp function of a threshold that has
to be derived from data.

**This PR does not change the default.** Swapping `Clusterer` for
`CorrelationClusterer` is a separate change with its own blast radius (serialized
`resolver.json` manifests name the clusterer class). This ships the measurement.

One correction worth flagging while citing it: the shipped pivot order is
**deterministic** (`sorted` by highest incident score, ties by node id), not the
uniformly *random* pivot of Ailon–Charikar–Newman that
`core/clusterers/correlation.py`'s docstring names — so ACN's 3-approximation
guarantee does not transfer to this implementation. Good for the harness (the
correlation column is exactly reproducible, no seed needed), but nothing above is
evidence for an approximation bound. The source docstring is out of this PR's
scope to edit; flagged as a follow-up.

### The two traps, counted rather than assumed

1. **Not `score < threshold`.** The `JudgementLog` v4 row schema persists no
   `threshold` column. Edges are rebuilt from **`verdict == True`** — the value
   `LoggingMatcher` got from `predicted_match(j, clusterer.threshold)`, the same
   predicate `Clusterer.cluster()` calls.
2. **`predicted_match` gives `decision` precedence over `score`**
   (`core/models.py:176-190`). Not hypothetical:
   `core/matchers/llm_judge.py:165` returns
   `ParsedVerdict(decision=..., score=None)`, so on an LLM run a score scan has
   no score to compare.

Three instrument checks run per benchmark, and each **raises** rather than
reporting a number it cannot vouch for:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `verdict_agreement` — recompute `predicted_match` from each row's own `score`/`decision`, compare to the logged `verdict` | **1.000 on all 9** (730,721 rows on `dblp_scholar`) |
| `reconstruction_exact` — re-cluster the rebuilt edges, compare partitions | **`true` on all 9** |
| sweep-vs-tuned-point — the grid sweep re-clusters the same judgements, so its entry at the tuned threshold must equal the tuned count | **exact on all 9** |
| `decider_override_rows` — rows a naive `score < threshold` scan would mis-flag, **both directions** | **0** — rapidfuzz emits `decision: null`, so trap 2 is **latent here, not absent** |

---

## B2 — is the benchmark portfolio trustworthy?

**No registered benchmark is saturated for the free string method.** On every
dataset where the comparison can be made honestly, `rapidfuzz` sits **0.09–0.69
F1 below** the published number. The portfolio's problem is the opposite of
saturation.

| benchmark | task | wheel-loadable | records | gold pairs | prevalence | max gold cluster | sep AUC | vocab Jaccard | min token coverage | x-src ceiling | rapidfuzz F1 | published F1 | **saturated** | **structural caveats** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `abt_buy` | linkage | no | 2,173 | 1,044 | 4.42e-04 | 3 | 0.957 | 0.322 | 0.796 | 0.9847 | 0.2018 | 0.893 (Ditto) | **no** | — |
| `amazon_google` | linkage | no | 4,589 | 1,390 | 1.32e-04 | 6 | 0.955 | 0.338 | 0.791 | **0.8396** | 0.2881 | 0.756 (Ditto) | **no** | **capped-recall** |
| `dblp_acm` | linkage | no | 4,910 | 2,220 | 1.84e-04 | 2 | 1.000 | 0.842 | 0.967 | 1.0000 | 0.8905 | ~0.98 | **no** (gap 0.09) | † strictly 1:1 labels |
| `dblp_scholar` | linkage | no | 66,879 | 13,763 | 6.15e-06 | **37** | 0.993 | **0.061** | 0.651 | **0.3977** | 0.6588 | not recorded | **?** | **capped-recall**, **large-component** |
| `walmart_amazon` | linkage | no | 24,628 | 1,092 | 3.60e-06 | 4 | 0.996 | 0.133 | 0.806 | **0.8837** | 0.3051 | not recorded | **?** | **capped-recall** |
| `wdc_computers` | linkage | no | 4,647 | 1,111 | 1.03e-04 | 4 | 0.929 | 0.720 | 0.978 | **0.9001** | 0.4447 | not recorded | **?** | **capped-recall** |
| `fodors_zagat` | linkage | **yes** | 864 | **112** | 3.00e-04 | 2 | 0.998 | 0.285 | 0.708 | 1.0000 | no lit. split | 1.00 (ZeroER) | † **YES** | **tiny-gold** |
| `febrl_person` | linkage | **yes** | 1,000 | 500 | 1.00e-03 | 2 | 1.000 | 0.682 | 0.851 | 1.0000 | no lit. split | not recorded | **?** | **1:1 by construction** |
| `tiny_fixture` | linkage | **yes** | 12 | 3 | 4.55e-02 | 2 | 0.989 | 0.269 | 0.447 | 1.0000 | 0.0000 | n/a | n/a | tiny-gold, lexical-gap |
| `opensanctions` | linkage | no | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | **?** | external-only (CC-BY-NC, not vendored) |

**† = written by hand, not produced by the harness** (the doc names all four and
says why). Everything unmarked is a rendering of `portfolio_profile.json`.

**Which failed to load:** only `opensanctions`, and it is `loadable=False` by
registration — external-only, CC-BY-NC, deliberately not vendored. **Nothing is
broken.** The harness distinguishes that from a wheel exclusion, which is the
`wheel-loadable` column: `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.hatch.build] exclude` drops
the corpora for six registered sets, so **only 3 of the 9 loadable benchmarks
can be loaded from a `pip install`** — the rest exist only in a git checkout.

### Four benchmarks cannot reach recall 1.0, by construction

A two-source linkage pipeline pairs A-records against B-records, so **no
candidate set it can produce contains an intra-source pair** — and every gold
cluster spanning 3+ records emits some. Those gold pairs are unreachable before
any method runs. Now computed for every entry as the `x-src recall ceiling`
column:

| benchmark | ceiling | unreachable gold pairs | max gold cluster |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amazon_google` | **0.8396** | 16.0 % | 6 |
| `walmart_amazon` | **0.8837** | 11.6 % | 4 |
| `wdc_computers` | **0.9001** | 10.0 % | 4 |
| `abt_buy` | 0.9847 | 1.5 % | 3 |
| `dblp_scholar` | **0.3977** | **60.2 %** | 37 |
| the four 1:1 sets | 1.0000 | 0 % | 2 |

A blocker scoring 0.84 recall on `amazon_google` is not at 84 % of the task — it
is at **100.0 % of what is reachable**. Reporting it against 1.0 invents a
16-point gap no engineering can close, and any optimizer maximizing recall there
spends its whole budget chasing it.

This is `dblp_scholar`'s 37-record component generalized: same phenomenon, same
arithmetic, measured portfolio-wide. Stream A derived the same four ceilings from
a completely separate candidate-recall harness; this reproduces them exactly from
the gold labels alone.

It also flags a live claim in shipped source — `src/langres/optimize.py:135-139`
asserts all gold matches are inter-source. False on four of nine loadable
benchmarks, and false for the *majority* of gold pairs on `dblp_scholar`. Out of
scope here (a source fix with its own blast radius); this is the measurement that
settles it.

**Portfolio-level gaps:**
- **All 10 registered entries are `task="linkage"`. There is no registered
  dedup benchmark** — the V1 use case with no measurement.
- Named in docs but never registered: WDC Products, Beer, iTunes-Amazon, Alaska,
  Machamp, matchbench.
- `fodors_zagat` is saturated **on BCubed** (112 gold pairs, 1:1, ZeroER at
  1.00) — confirmed; the verdict names its metric.
- DBLP-Scholar's 37-record connected component is confirmed as a
  transitive-closure labeling artifact — and the composition settles it: derived
  by an independent path (stdlib `csv` + union-find over the raw label files,
  importing no langres code, reproducing 2,351 components and the largest at 37
  exactly), that component holds **2 records from table A and 35 from table B**.
  It is not 37 papers; it is two DBLP entries chained through 35 Scholar records.

---

## The instrument was checked before it was trusted

Six values reproduced **exactly** against numbers already recorded in `docs/`:
`fodors_zagat` 112 gold pairs · `dblp_scholar` 66,879 records / 2,351 clusters /
13,763 closure pairs / 37-record largest component · `walmart_amazon` 846
clusters + 22,820 singletons / 1,092 pairs · `wdc_computers` 877 clusters / 1,111
pairs · `dblp_acm` 2,220 strictly-1:1 clusters · `febrl_person` 500 pairs 1:1.

Plus an independent cross-check on the wheel column: `wheel_status()` derives it
from `pyproject.toml`'s globs, `tests/test_wheel_contents.py::SHIPPED_NON_PY_FILES`
derives it from the **real built artifacts** — a test asserts the two agree, so a
stale glob cannot silently reach the annotation.

---

## New source: `VocabularyOverlapSection`

The one B2 measurement `DataProfileReport` did not already compute (every other
quantity was re-verified against the code, not inherited from the agenda).
Token-type Jaccard + overlap coefficient, occurrence-weighted per-side coverage,
and the most-shared tokens between the **two sources** of a linkage corpus.

Follows the existing section contract: `ProfileSection` subclass, `rows()` /
`panels()` / `to_dict()`, and **graceful degradation** — no two-valued `source`
field means no section, never an error (`source_key=` overrides the field name).

`tests/test_import_tangle.py` baseline raised 9 → 10. This is the
"prefer breaking the coupling" case where the new module cannot break it: the
knot's root is the pre-existing `base <-> builders` 2-cycle, and all seven
existing sections are already in that SCC for the same structural reason. The
comment on the baseline records the mechanism and that no other component grew.

---

## Verification

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pytest -m "not integration and not slow and not finetune"` | see below |
| `pytest -m "not integration and not finetune" --cov-report=xml` (90 % repo gate) | see below |
| `coverage report --include="src/langres/core/*,…" --fail-under=98` | see below |
| `ruff format --check .` | 561 files already formatted |
| `ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| `mypy src` | Success: no issues found in 215 source files |

Both harnesses were re-run end-to-end over every loadable benchmark and
reproduce.

## One library behaviour change: a real defect in `data_profile/builders.py`

**This is the only change in the PR that alters shipped library behaviour**, and
it is a genuine defect rather than fallout from the diagnostic — it affects
anyone profiling data with mixed-type source keys, whether or not they ever run
these harnesses.

`from_records` grouped sources by `str(value)`. Two *distinct* source values with
the same display form — the int `1` and the str `"1"` — therefore collapsed into
one key, so the documented "exactly two distinct values" condition silently
failed and the vocabulary-overlap section was dropped with no error. The fix
groups by the raw value and converts only the final display labels, falling back
to `repr` when two values render identically. Covered by
`test_two_sources_that_render_alike_are_not_collapsed` and
`test_a_single_source_under_two_spellings_still_yields_two_sides`.

Coverage, stated explicitly rather than left to be wondered about:
`src/langres/data/data_profile/*` sits **outside** the 98 % include list in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`, so this fix is gated by the 90 % repo-wide floor,
not the 98 % core gate. Both are green.

## What the automated reviews changed

Three rounds of Codex review found **ten** issues; **all ten are fixed** (the
last two in `f8ff3d6`). The two most valuable are the same failure shape this
repo keeps hitting — *a check decoupled from what it claims to check*:

1. **The instrument's own gate was circular.** `reconstruction_exact` replayed
   `Clusterer.cluster()` to verify a partition `Clusterer.cluster()` had produced,
   so it could not detect the predicate drift it existed to catch — and the other
   two gates were blind to the merge predicate as well (one validates the *log*,
   the sweep re-clusters through the same clusterer). Check B now rebuilds the
   partition with a **local union-find over the logged verdicts**, importing no
   langres clusterer. The whole nine-benchmark run was then redone against it:
   **no reported quantity changed** (0 differences beyond 1e-12; 9 float
   last-digit gaps at max 1.11e-16). That re-run is the point — before the fix,
   "the numbers agree" was a tautology.
2. **A narrowed run could destroy the canonical artifact.** `--out` defaulted to
   the tracked results path while `--fast`/`--only` measure a *subset* and the
   write replaces the file wholesale — so the reproduce command this very PR
   recommended would have cut the tracked nine-benchmark JSON to three. The code
   had a comment anticipating exactly this and only *warned*. Both harnesses now
   refuse: `parser.error` before any benchmark runs, an error when `--only`
   selects nothing, and `write_findings` will not put `[]` over a real result set.

Also fixed: the recall-ceiling column was described as bounding F1 (it bounds
recall/PC at `r` and F1 at the higher `2r/(1+r)` — 0.8396 permits 0.9128); a
wrong singleton contract (`VectorBlocker` emits 43 accepted self-pairs on
`amazon_google`, which become one-node components — verified in the log); a stale
instrument summary; a "randomized pivot" claim contradicting the same doc's §3.3;
and a §9 conclusion contradicting the new `capped-recall` tags.

### The transferable lesson, as a number: 30 % of findings were fix-induced

**Three of the ten findings were defects introduced by an earlier round's fix.**
Two arose in round 2 from round 1's fixes; one arose in round 3 from round 2's.
That is a **30 % fix-induced defect rate** across this PR's review history.

The round-3 case is the sharpest, and worth stating precisely: **the round-2 fix
for the canonical-artifact data-safety P1 introduced a crash.** Adding
`CANONICAL_OUT` as the `--out` default left the final write still passing
`args.out`, which is `None` on a full run — so a fix written to stop the tool
destroying a 13-minute result set instead made the documented full-portfolio
command die with `AttributeError` on `out.parent` *after* every measurement had
completed. A data-safety fix that creates a crash is the whole argument in one
example.

The consequence is procedural and it is the most portable thing here: **a fix
round is new code and needs review like any other.** It is not a privileged edit
that lands clean by virtue of being a fix. The only reason these surfaced is that
review was re-requested after *every* fix round rather than the head being
assumed good — and the final round caught a P1 that CI, `mypy`, `ruff` and three
rounds of self-review had all passed over. Pyright had in fact flagged the exact
line (`Argument of type "Any | None" … "None" is not assignable to "Path"`) and
it was skimmed past by everyone who looked, including me.

### The last two findings, and how they were closed

Both came from round 3, both were verified against the code rather than taken on
trust, and both are fixed in `f8ff3d6`:

- **P1 — `closure_diagnostic.py:925` passed `args.out` instead of the resolved
  `out`.** Fixed. The committed results were never at risk: the per-benchmark
  write inside the loop always passed the resolved path, which is *why* the
  failure only struck at the very end, and why the artifact in this PR is valid.
  `portfolio_profile.py` was checked and does not share the bug.
- **P2 — the narrowed-run guard test asserted the exit code, not the ordering.**
  Fixed. It now spies on `run_benchmark` and `write_findings` and requires that
  **neither ran**, so moving the guard below the benchmark loop fails the test.
  Previously `SystemExit(2)` alone would have kept it green while the canonical
  artifact was already being rewritten — the same false-green pattern this PR
  documents elsewhere.

**The P1 regression test was confirmed to fail against the unfixed code before
the fix was applied**, and for the right reason: the recorded writes were
`[PosixPath('…/closure_diagnostic.json'), None]` — in-loop call correct, final
call `None`. It pins the **last** write specifically, because a test asserting
merely that *some* write received a `Path` would have passed against the bug.

## What the pre-PR self-review changed (and one wrong published number it caught)

Both files went through a focused correctness review before this PR opened. The
findings that mattered:

**A real measurement bug, now fixed and re-run.** `DataProfileReport.from_benchmark`
builds records with `model_dump()`, and pydantic v2 **includes computed fields** —
every vendored ER schema defines `embed_text` as a *concatenation of other fields
on the same record* (`AbtBuySchema.embed_text == name + " " + description`). The
vocabulary section tokenized the dump as-is, so it counted the blocking text
twice: over-weighting exactly the fields a blocker reads in an
occurrence-weighted measure, and disagreeing with the separability signal in the
adjacent column, which iterates `model_fields` and never sees a computed field.

Type Jaccard was unaffected (a derived field's tokens are a subset of the fields
it concatenates). Coverage moved where `embed_text` joins more than one field:
`abt_buy` 0.795→0.796, `amazon_google` 0.793→0.791, `febrl_person` 0.838→0.851,
`fodors_zagat` 0.702→0.708, `walmart_amazon` 0.798→0.806; `dblp_acm`,
`dblp_scholar`, `wdc_computers`, `tiny_fixture` unchanged. **No verdict changed.**
The whole profile was regenerated and §6 of the annotation records the correction
rather than quietly absorbing it.

**Gates that could not fail, now able to.**
- The instrument checks logged an error and then reported the number anyway, and
  neither appeared in the rendered table — a valid run and an invalidated one
  were byte-identical to a reader. They now raise. (This repo's own documented
  failure mode: a green light decoupled from what it checks.)
- Added a free third check: the sweep re-clusters the same judgements, so its
  entry at the tuned threshold must equal the tuned count. Two code paths, one
  number.
- `test_source_label_is_excluded_from_the_vocabulary` asserted a label was absent
  from the *shared*-token list — where it can never appear by construction — so it
  passed identically with the exclusion removed. It now asserts the numbers the
  leak moves.
- Only 1 of the 4 rules deciding a published verdict was pinned to its value; the
  rest were referenced symbolically, so redefining one would have rewritten the
  annotation with a green suite. All four are pinned.
- The citation test checked only that the cited *file* exists. It now reads the
  cited line and asserts the number is on it — which surfaced that
  `PUBLISHED_SOTA["dblp_acm"].system` attributed "DeepMatcher family" to a line
  that names no system at all. Removed.

**Honesty fixes.** Four cells in the annotation table were hand-written in
columns the doc tells the reader are code-derived; they now carry a `†` and a
paragraph saying which and why. The `decider_override_rows` counter counted only
one of the two directions the naive scan gets wrong. The `large-component` rule
fired on any task, though it reads a big cluster as a *two-source* closure
artifact — now scoped to `linkage`, so the dedup benchmark §7 asks for won't be
branded on arrival. A crashed saturation measurement was indistinguishable from
"ships no literature split"; there is now a `saturation_error` field.

I did **not** act on: the pre-existing `base ↔ builders` import cycle (the real
root of the tangle bump — out of scope, and unpicking it is its own PR); the
`one-to-one` rule's treatment of singletons (the rule was fixed before looking;
widening it now to make one cell computed would be exactly the post-hoc move the
protocol forbids — the cell is marked manual instead); and the double corpus load
in `profile_entry` (a perf nit on a $0 harness).

- **`docs/BENCHMARKS.md` is not updated.** It is the natural home for the

- **The clusterer default is unchanged** (see B1 (c) above).

## Reproducing

```bash
uv run python examples/research/portfolio_profile.py     # B2
uv run python examples/research/closure_diagnostic.py    # B1, 639 s of compute
uv run python examples/research/closure_diagnostic.py --fast --out tmp/fast.json   # 27 s
```

A narrowed run (`--fast`/`--only`) must name its own `--out`: the write replaces
the results file wholesale, so aiming a subset at the canonical path would shrink
the tracked nine-benchmark artifact. The CLI refuses rather than warning.
